title: Adjacency map for trace tags and dashboard onramp
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note to sketch an adjacency-style map that ties together trace tag choices, minimal dashboard tiles for rapid investigation, and a lightweight onboarding checklist for new model rollouts. Goal is to reduce time-to-first-deck for oncall and surface the common investigative paths we want operators to take.

Audience:
- Obs engineers building trace instrumentation
- Dashboard authors and operator UX owners
- SREs and oncall who will use the artifacts during incidents

Problem statement (short):
We often instrument traces without clarity on which dashboard panels are expected to answer each trace-level question. When an anomaly occurs, operators spin up ad-hoc queries, rebuild panels, or hand off to instrument owners. This doc proposes an adjacency map (tag -> trace slices -> panels/queries) and a minimal onboarding checklist so rollouts include both traces and a small set of dashboard tiles.

High-level approach:
1) Define a small, consistent tag grammar: purpose, dimension, provenance
   - purpose: what the instrumentation is for (latency, cache, fallback, quality)
   - dimension: tenant, model, route, sequence_length_bucket
   - provenance: service, runtime (host/vm/gpu-pool), client-sdk-version
2) For each tag or tag-group, enumerate 2–3 investigative queries and the 1–2 dashboard tiles that should exist for fast triage.
3) Provide a rollout checklist so product/infra owners include tags + tiles before enabling new model variants.

Tag grammar (proposal):
- obs.purpose = {latency, cost, cache, fallback, quality, error}
- obs.dim = {tenant_id, model_id, route, seq_bucket}
- obs.source = {ingress, runtime, sidecar, client}
- obs.variant = {quant, fp16, int8, baseline}
- obs.op = {kv_hit, kv_miss, batch_size, prefetch}

Naming hints (compact examples):
- obs.purpose=latency;obs.dim=model_id:mixgrow-13b;obs.op=kv_miss
- obs.purpose=cache;obs.dim=tenant_id:1234;obs.source=runtime

Adjacency map examples (compact):
1) Tag group: latency + model_id + seq_bucket
   - Investigator questions: which model & sequence length are slow? is latency dominated in runtime or in pre/post-processing?
   - Quick queries: p95 latency by model_id and seq_bucket; breakdown runtime_vs_client_latency by model_id
   - Dashboard tiles to create: small heatmap (model x seq bucket) with p50/p95; stacked bar for runtime vs preproc latencies

2) Tag group: cache (kv_miss) + tenant_id
   - Investigator questions: are cold caches causing tail latency or increased cost? which tenants suffer most?
   - Quick queries: kv_miss rate by tenant, tail latency for requests with kv_miss vs kv_hit
   - Dashboard tiles: tenant-ranked list with miss-rate and tail-latency; drilldown link to sample traces for top N tenants

3) Tag group: fallback + route + source=ingress
   - Investigator questions: are fallbacks triggered by model errors or by routing rules?
   - Quick queries: fallback counts by route and error class; fraction of responses served by fallback model over time
   - Dashboard tiles: time-series of fallback % (per-route selector) and alertable anomaly detector on sudden increases

Minimal dashboard onramp checklist (for every model/rollout):
- [ ] Confirm the model_id tag is emitted on every request span
- [ ] Ensure obs.purpose is set for spans where relevant (latency/cache/fallback)
- [ ] Create two small tiles: "model x seq heatmap (p95)" and "runtime/preproc breakdown (p95)" with links to sample traces
- [ ] Add a tenant-ranked miss-rate tile if model is multi-tenant
- [ ] Create a short playbook snippet (1–2 bullets) pinned on the dashboard with the top 3 queries to run next

Operator UX notes / micro-templates:
- Tile captions should include the minimal trace query and an explicit link to "open sample traces". Example caption: "p95 by model/seq_bucket — click to view worst 5 traces (query id: obs-query-314)."
- Avoid over-aggregation on the first page; give operators the ability to expand to cohorted views (tenant/model/route).
- Pre-save 3 trace-sample queries per tile: worst-by-latency, worst-by-cost, worst-by-eviction

Lightweight trace query snippets (pseudo-sql / DSL):
- p95_latency_by_model_seq: SELECT model_id, seq_bucket, quantile(0.95, latency_ms) FROM spans WHERE obs.purpose='latency' GROUP BY model_id, seq_bucket
- kv_miss_tail_by_tenant: SELECT tenant_id, quantile(0.99, latency_ms) FROM spans WHERE obs.op='kv_miss' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 50

Onboarding process (stages):
- Stage 0 (pre-rollout): authors confirm tags in dev traces and add tile stubs in a staging dashboard
- Stage 1 (canary): enable tags in canary path, verify dashboards populate, smoke-run the 3 saved queries
- Stage 2 (GA): finalize tiles, add playbook bullets, and label dashboard owner

Open questions / tradeoffs (callouts):
- Tag cardinality: obs.dim=tenant_id can be high cardinality. Proposal: emit tenant_id at span-level but only use as a group-by in investigation mode; dashboards should default to top-N only.
- Tag mutation patterns: how do we handle model aliases and version renames? Need canonical model_id registry and lightweight shim that maps aliases in traces.
- Sample storage cost: storing samples for all tiles can be expensive. Consider time-limited pinned traces (keep 5 worst per tile for 48h)

Action items (next steps / owners):
- Jonah: prototype a dashboard template and pre-saved queries for the three adjacency examples (due: 2025-03-10)
- Marta: spike on alias-to-model_id registry and propose small API for instrumentation (due: 2025-03-14)
- Devon: cost estimate for trace-sample retention policy and quota proposal (due: 2025-03-12)

Notes to self / TODO fragments:
- Add a small example screenshot and query ids once Jonah has the template.
- Need to run this by product-hosted-api for naming convention alignment.
- Consider adding a "mini-playbook" widget that surfaces the 3 investigation queries and a one-click link to open the sample traces viewer.

References and links:
- Confluence: OBS-ADJMAP-42 (high-level proposal)
- Jira: OBS-789 (instrumentation epic)
- Existing deck: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/PR-214

Status: draft — want feedback on tag grammar and on the minimal onramp checklist.

End.
